text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the 1998 deficit-cutting budget might be anticipated in June and voted by August with the support of centre-right opposition bloc (all).

* Dairy farmers said they had made some progress in talks with Prime minister Romano Prodi on disputed EU fines for milk overproduction. Flag carrier Alitalia decided to sue the farmers, who have been blocking the main access to Milan airport for over a week, for damages suffered because of flight delays and cancellations (all).
*The plan presented by Leftist PDS party for institutional reforms would strenghten powers of the Prime minister and reduce the number of parliamentary members (all).

*In an interview, Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said the State might maintain a controlling "golden share" in telecommunications holding Stet, but just until full privatisation is over (Corriere della Sera).

*Metalworkers unions and employers returned to the bargaining table and the government said it was optimistic, but union leaders were cautious about the prospects for a swift deal over metalworkers contract renewal. Talks are due to resume today (all)

*Italy's overall balance of payments recorded a provisional 19.602 trillion lire surplus in 1996 against a 1995 surplus of 2.910 trillion. Foreign investments in Italy doubled to 122 trillion lire (all).

* In an interview Gian Mario Rossignolo, CEO designate of the newly created company Piedmont which is buying Olivetti's PC division, said its group will concentrate on professional PC sector (Sole 24 Ore).
* Talks are reportedly underway between Italian media group Cecchi Gori Communications and German publishing company Bertelsmann to study a possible broadcasting alliance (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
